text.inkscape:label: Header Text
text.tspan: Deltalazer Branding Guidelines
You can edit this file with Inkscape!
Yahallo Inkscape user [or SVG reader idk]!
This text is JUST FOR YOU!
Made by KarstenPH
Additional Items:
Usage Guidelines:

You must inform us of any use of the logo, for any projects, under the official Discord server, or through the "Discussions" tab of the delta/delta-resources repository [With the "Usage Request" flair].
This is compulsory, unless the logo is an accessory to a wider project (e.g. A video, a project, etc.)
It may not be mandatory, but doing things this way minimizes conflict.
If we do not reply within 7 days, you may proceed under the assumption of acceptance, however we may request for the adjustment or removal of any infringing assets *for said version*.

As detailed in Section 2 (see above), Additions to the logo require explicit provided approval by the DeltaLazer team. Once we approve of a use, we will not revoke permission for that for that specific release of your project.
We do, however, reserve the right to request changes or removal for any future revisions or updates.

These visual assets are licensed under CC BY-NC, meaning you can use it for any and all non-commercial purposes. [This, however, does not constitute legal advice. Go to the root directory of this repository to learn more.]
The Quicksand font is subject to it's own SIL Open Font License.
Please see it's original license file under https://github.com/andrew-paglinawan/QuicksandFamily/blob/master/OFL.txt for more details

Flow maps

See top right corner of this document for more info
Please note: The Alpha and flow maps do NOT follow
the outline of the logo 1:1
This is because of an oversight caused by the design.
When you overlap the final symbol to the timemap
and compare the outlines, they are slightly different.
This is because the logo's margins are too small,
and that requires further adjustment that will likely take days
[since you'd need to rebuild the logo like a few times]
How to Edge (mask):
1. Copy the edgemask layer
2. Open a new inkscape instance.
3. Paste the layer in [Yes, you can do this]
4. Save as .sif
5. Open in Synfig
6. Add gradients into Element layers
7. Organize as necessary
8. Duplicate the layer you finished 3 times
9. Put 3/4 of those layers into a group folder
10. Export each header folder separately

For Public Release
Version 2026.04.10 | UTC Based Metric
Please don't disable Project Anti-aliasing!
There are also a few common rules you should follow across ALL logos:
All logos MUST be sharp at all times. In certain circumstances however, such as application icons, it may be acceptable to have reduced quality.
[This is (mostly) only allowed if it is caused by your environment and not by the source. Example: Desktop Enivornment Taskbar or Floating Icon]
Ensure that there is no visual clutter when adding any additional Elements. Use visual balancing tools to ensure that the design is consistent.
Ensure that the logo maintains a high contrast with its background. This means, it must be completely visible. If the logo you selected IS NOT completely visible, you are required to switch Variants.
Always use the most up-to-date assets provided in the repository, under the master branch.
Avoid using any assets from the experimental branch. The assets you should be using are found *within this SVG file*, and NOT on the textures directory.
If you want pre-rendered images, they are also available inside of this folder.
⚠️ DO NOT Modify the composition of the Logo in the following ways:
DO NOT remove or alter the styling of the Unit
Do not alter the Outer ring
Do not remove the Stylized Symbol
delta
Do not modify the logo's in-fill
More info about this can be found higher up in the document
Scaling is not part of transformation
DO NOT Transform the unit
Do not alter the Aspect Ratio
Do not Rotate The Unit
Only applies for static appearances
DO NOT Apply any special effects
Do not apply surface material effects
Do not use effects that impair visibility
Exception:
You may append additions to all logo variants that are not the Mini Logo, however the font MUST MATCH.
Any additions done here require DIRECT APPROVAL from us, as these modifications modify the core logo.
These additions must NOT subtract any elements from the Logo Unit.
lazer - community
Do not make modifications to the text in any way, shape, or form.
A. DO NOT move the location of the text
B. DO NOT Apply stretching effects
C. DO NOT resize the text independently of the Unit
(the text must always remain the exact same size relative to the outer ring).
D. DO NOT change the font, or it's weight.
E. DO NOT alter the spacing between the letters (kerning/tracking). [Note that spacing will likely change for future iterations]
F. DO NOT warp, bend, arc, or slant the text.
⚠️ DO NOT Modify the text Element of the logo in any way, shape or form, outside of the allowed color modifications per logo.
deltΔ
lazer
In order for the logo to be distinct, it must always be given adequate breathing room,
and should never collide with surrounding elements or edges.
The logo should typically occupy 75-95% of its maximum available space within its container,
leaving the remaining area as a protective margin, however this is not a hard limit.
For reference, you may duplicate it and shrink the duplicate to fit within the *inner* portion of the outer ring.
Main Logo

text.inkscape:label: Text Unit
text.tspan: This is the primary logo variant should be used under all normal circumstances.
Prohibitions:
1. You may not modify the color of the infill, in any way, shape or form.
2. You MUST NOT Remove the infill [as in: Creating an effective replica of the Single Color variant]
3. You ABSOLUTELY MUST NOT Remove any part of the Element.

text.inkscape:label: Text Unit
text.tspan: This variant is only to be used for Elements that are typically smaller than exactly 1.5 inches [Guideline: You can use your thumb to measure this].
There is no hard minimum size, however the Element must, at the very least, be clearly legible to the human eye.
Please note that this document purposefully does NOT include Pixel-based sizing guidelines, as resolutions are not a fixed metric and can vary.
PPI is, however, which is why the Inch is the metric of measurement used here.
Prohibitions:
You may not remove any of its Elements, outside of the fill.
In the case where you DO remove the fill, This logo's rules become identical to the single color variant.
Single Color

text.inkscape:label: Text Unit
text.tspan: This Variant may only have three color Variations.
- Monotone White, Black, or Any Color variation of Red [Bright, or Dim]
- A Gradient consisting of red with a continuously varying intensity
Prohibitions:
1. You should not change the color to anything that isn't listed above
2. You should not add a gradient that does not use Red [Such as Blue to Green]
3. You should not add a gradient that is non continuous [Gradients that Repeat Directly or through Reflection] or non-linear
4. You should not add an In-fill that specifically covers the inner mask of the logo [as in: Creating an effective replica of the Main variant]
5. You should not turn the Element into a mask for any artwork
If you do not use White or Black, You may deviate from pure Red by adding a small amount of Green and Blue.

A good rule of thumb is that the value changes relative to how bright your Red channel is. For example: If Red is 255 under the RGB spectrum, you may add a brightness of 50 for any of the other channels maximum.
In order to get your limit, simply multiply your Red channel to 0.196.
Example: 255 x 0.196 = 50, meaning your maximum allowed G and B values are both 50. 200 x 0.196 = 39, meaning your maximum allowed G and B values are both 39
If you ever get an uneven value, always round downward.
Single Color

- Section 2: The Logo

text.inkscape:label: Text Unit
text.tspan: This document refers to the logo in a few ways, and the two terms are very similar. to clear up some confusion, these are the definitions:.
Logo Units refer to the overall composition of the logos.
The Elements refer to the form of the logo, which include the text, and the rings, while excluding additional items like the background image.
Each individual logo has its own separate rules to follow.
- Section 1: The name

text.inkscape:label: Text Unit 2
text.tspan: deltalazer / DELTALAZER (with no capitalization or full capitalization)
DeltaLazer (using PascalCase, also known as UpperCamelCase)
Delta Lazer / delta lazer (as separate nouns, with and without capitalization)
In this document, the definition of "Official Usage" refers to any use of the project name outside of explicit parody, comedy, satire/memes, or casual usage [e.g. discussions]

text.inkscape:label: Text Unit 1
text.tspan: When referring to this project with any official capacity, you can only refer to deltalazer in these three ways:
This document sets standards for the usage of the name "deltalazer" and its associated logos.
